name: Plains
notes: Mana ability is intrinsic to the basic land type; the oracle text is reminder text only. land_types is load-bearing downstream: the Onslaught fetchlands search by land type rather than by the word basic, and the Torment Tainted cycle checks for a Swamp by type. Anything carrying the type satisfies them regardless of card name.

name: Island
notes: See Plains. Intrinsic ability from the basic land type.

name: Swamp
notes: See Plains. The Tainted cycle keys off this land type, so Snow-Covered Swamp satisfies it identically.

name: Mountain
notes: See Plains. Intrinsic ability from the basic land type.

name: Forest
notes: See Plains. Intrinsic ability from the basic land type.

name: City of Brass

other_abilities.effect: Deals 1 damage to you whenever this land becomes tapped.

notes: The damage is a triggered ability on becoming tapped, not a cost on the mana ability. Three consequences a calculator should not blur together: the mana ability itself is free and unconditional, so this is a genuine untapped five-colour source on turn one; the damage cannot be declined or routed around by paying differently; and it fires on any tap for any reason, including taps by opponents' effects and taps for abilities that are not mana abilities. Contrast the Ice Age painlands, where the damage is part of one specific ability's effect and the colourless mode avoids it entirely.

name: Oasis

other_abilities.effect: Prevent the next 1 damage that would be dealt to target creature this turn.

notes: Produces no mana at all. Kept in the file with an empty abilities array rather than omitted, so a calculator reading a decklist counts it as a land that is not a mana source instead of failing the lookup and guessing. Any consumer computing coloured sources should iterate abilities, which is empty here, not assume every land contributes.

name: Mishra's Factory

other_abilities.effect: Becomes a 2/2 Assembly-Worker artifact creature until end of turn. Still a land.
Target Assembly-Worker creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

notes: Colourless only; never a source of coloured mana. Animation costs {1} and does not tap it, so it can be animated and still tapped for mana the same turn. The pump ability costs {T} and competes directly with the mana ability, so a turn spent pumping is a turn this land produces nothing.

name: Urza's Mine
notes: One printed ability whose amount changes, split into two entries so a consumer can select the highest-amount entry whose condition holds. The entries are mutually exclusive, not cumulative. The condition is on land types, not card names, and the subtype is hyphenated as Urza's Power-Plant while the card is named Urza's Power Plant. Matching on card name fails silently here, which is exactly the kind of thing that ships a bug.

name: Urza's Power Plant
notes: See Urza's Mine. Card name has no hyphen, land type does.

name: Urza's Tower
notes: See Urza's Mine. Tower is the only one of the three that goes to 3, so assembled Tron is 7 colourless, not 6.

name: Safe Haven

other_abilities.effect: Exile target creature you control.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may sacrifice this land to return each card it exiled to the battlefield under its owner's control.

notes: Produces no mana. It does leave play under its own power, but only through an optional upkeep trigger unrelated to mana. This is why other_abilities carries its own sacrifices_self flag: the per-ability flag inside abilities would have nowhere to live on a card with no mana ability, and the fetchlands later have the same shape.

name: Ruins of Trokair
notes: Legal through Fifth and Classic Sixth Edition reprints; the Fallen Empires printing recorded in first_printing is the oldest, not the legal one. Enters tapped, so it produces nothing the turn it lands and is never a turn-one white source. The sacrifice mode is the point: two mana on the turn you need it, at the cost of the land. Compare the storage cycle from the same set, which reaches a similar total by charging over several turns instead of paying the land up front.

notes: See Ruins of Trokair. Same cycle, blue.

name: Icatian Store

abilities.cost: {T}, Remove any number of storage counters

variable_amount.accrual: one counter at the beginning of each of your upkeeps while this land is tapped

other_abilities.effect: You may choose not to untap this land during your untap step.
At the beginning of your upkeep, if this land is tapped, put a storage counter on it.

notes: amount is 0 because with no counters this taps for nothing, and 0 is the safe default: a consumer that ignores variable_amount will undercount rather than promise mana that isn't there. Charging is not free. A counter arrives at upkeep only if the land is tapped, so each stored mana costs a full turn of the land producing nothing, and cashing in requires untapping first, which means no counter is added on the turn you spend it. This is a battery, not a land with a per-turn rate.

name: Adarkar Wastes
notes: Two separate abilities, not one ability with a rider. The colourless mode is free of damage, which is why these are not simply worse City of Brass: a deck using one for generic costs pays nothing. The 1 damage in the second ability is part of that ability's effect rather than a cost, so it cannot be declined once that mode is chosen, but choosing the colourless mode avoids it entirely. Damage source is the land, so it is damage and not life loss, which matters for prevention effects. Untapped, unconditional, unlimited: a real turn-one source of both its colours.

name: Underground River
notes: See Adarkar Wastes. Same cycle, blue and black.

name: Sulfurous Springs
notes: See Adarkar Wastes. Same cycle, black and red.

name: Karplusan Forest
notes: See Adarkar Wastes. Same cycle, red and green. Note the name contains Forest but the card has no Forest land type, so it is not fetchable and does not satisfy anything checking for a Forest.

name: Brushland

name: Land Cap

availability.reason: Tapping for mana puts a depletion counter on it. It does not untap on your next untap step because the counter is still there; the counter is removed at that turn's upkeep, by which point it is already past untapping. It untaps normally the turn after.

other_abilities.effect: Doesn't untap during your untap step if it has a depletion counter on it.
At the beginning of your upkeep, remove a depletion counter from this land.

notes: Enters untapped and has no activation cost, so on the turn you use it this is a clean dual source and it can be a turn-one coloured source. The cost is paid in tempo afterwards: usable on your first turn, then not your second, then yes your third. total_activations is null because the number of uses is unlimited over a long enough game; the constraint is rate, not total, and it lives in availability. A calculator that treats this as a plain dual land will overcount available mana on consecutive turns, which is the failure mode to watch.

availability.reason: See Land Cap. Depletion counter placed by the mana ability blocks the next untap step.

name: Glacial Chasm

other_abilities.effect: When this land enters, sacrifice a land.
Cumulative upkeep, pay 2 life.
Creatures you control can't attack.
Prevent all damage that would be dealt to you.

notes: Produces no mana and actively costs you mana: the enters trigger sacrifices a land, and it may be a different land, not this one, so sacrifices_self is false on that entry. Net effect on a mana base is minus two lands, this one and whatever it eats. The cumulative upkeep does eventually sacrifice it, hence sacrifices_self true on that entry. Any calculator counting lands in play needs the enters trigger or it will be one land high from the turn this resolves.

name: Halls of Mist

other_abilities.effect: Cumulative upkeep {1}.
Creatures that attacked during their controller's last turn can't attack.

notes: Produces no mana and drains it. The cumulative upkeep is paid in mana, so this is a negative mana source that gets worse every turn: {1} on the first upkeep, {2} on the second, and so on. Anything modelling available mana per turn should subtract, not ignore.

name: Ice Floe

other_abilities.effect: You may choose not to untap this land during your untap step.
Tap target creature without flying that's attacking you. It doesn't untap during its controller's untap step for as long as this land remains tapped.

notes: Produces no mana. The optional-untap clause exists to hold the lock down, not to store anything, so it has nothing in common with the Fallen Empires storage lands despite sharing that line of text. Reading that line as a storage mechanic is exactly the pattern-matching error this file exists to prevent.

name: Snow-Covered Plains
notes: Mana-identical to Plains. It carries the Plains land type, so it satisfies anything checking for that type and is a legal target for effects that search for a Plains card. The Snow supertype only matters to cards that specifically reference snow permanents; for mana purposes it changes nothing.

name: Snow-Covered Island
notes: See Snow-Covered Plains.

name: Snow-Covered Swamp
notes: See Snow-Covered Plains. Carries the Swamp type, so it turns on the Torment Tainted cycle exactly as a Swamp does.

name: Snow-Covered Mountain
notes: See Snow-Covered Plains.

name: Snow-Covered Forest
notes: See Snow-Covered Plains.

name: An-Havva Township
notes: This is the Skycloud Expanse trap in its worst form. Anything reading mana symbols records a green, red and white source. In play it is a colourless land that can convert: the green mode nets zero mana and the red or white mode actively loses one. Neither coloured mode is self-sufficient, so this can never be your first coloured source, and with this as your only land you cannot produce a single coloured mana at all. Count it as a colourless source that fixes late, never as fixing that enables a curve.

name: Aysen Abbey
notes: See An-Havva Township. Same cycle, white primary, green and blue secondary.

name: Castle Sengir
notes: See An-Havva Township. Same cycle, black primary, blue and red secondary.

name: Koskun Keep
notes: See An-Havva Township. Same cycle, red primary, black and green secondary.

name: Wizards' School
notes: See An-Havva Township. Same cycle, blue primary, white and black secondary.

name: Balduvian Trading Post

other_abilities.effect: Deals 1 damage to target attacking creature.

notes: Produces both mana every time, not a choice between them. This is the distinction the produces object exists for: {C}{R} is mode fixed with two symbols, while a painland's {W} or {U} is mode choice with one. Entry cost is a replacement effect, so it is paid before the land is ever on the battlefield and there is no window where you control it without having paid. If you cannot pay it never enters and goes to the graveyard, which costs you the land drop and the card. Net land count is unchanged, but you convert a Mountain into two mana a turn. The Mountain must be untapped, which is not true of every member of this cycle.

name: Soldevi Excavations

other_abilities.effect: Scry 1.

notes: See Balduvian Trading Post. Same shape, blue, and the Island must also be untapped.

name: Heart of Yavimaya

other_abilities.effect: Target creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

notes: Only one mana, unlike the Balduvian and Soldevi members of this cycle, so the Forest you eat is a straight downgrade in mana terms and you are paying for the pump ability. The Forest does not have to be untapped here, which is a real difference from Balduvian Trading Post and Soldevi Excavations and is easy to flatten if you read the cycle as uniform. The pump ability costs {T} and competes with the mana ability.

name: Kjeldoran Outpost

other_abilities.effect: Create a 1/1 white Soldier creature token.

notes: See Heart of Yavimaya. One mana, Plains need not be untapped. The token ability costs {T} plus two mana, so on any turn you make a Soldier this land is a net drain of two, not a source.

name: Lake of the Dead
notes: The big ability sacrifices a Swamp, not itself, so sacrifices_self is false and additional_cost carries the real price. Lake of the Dead survives; your Swamp does not. It is repeatable as long as you keep feeding it Swamps, which is why it is not modelled as a one-shot. Entry cost eats a Swamp too, so getting to the four-mana turn costs two Swamps in total. Net mana on the turn you fire it is plus four, but land count drops by one each time and the file does not model that decay anywhere except here.

name: School of the Unseen
notes: Same family as the Homelands castles. Reads as a five-colour source and is not one: the coloured mode nets minus one and is not self-sufficient, so it can never be your first coloured mana and never accelerates you. It is a colourless land with an expensive late-game fixing button.

name: Sheltered Valley

other_abilities.effect: At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control three or fewer lands, you gain 1 life.

notes: The entry replacement is not a cost you can fail to pay, it is self-culling: playing a second copy sacrifices the first. Four copies in a deck are still at most one on the battlefield at any time. Any calculator that counts copies in a decklist as independent mana sources will overcount this card specifically, which is why entry_cost is populated even though nothing can go wrong when it enters.

name: Thawing Glaciers

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle. Return this land to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next cleanup step.

availability.reason: Returns itself to hand at the next cleanup, so replaying it uses your land drop every turn.

notes: Produces no mana itself, so abilities is empty. Three costs a naive reading misses. It enters tapped, so it cannot fetch the turn it lands. The fetched land arrives tapped, so it gives no mana that turn either. And it bounces itself every turn, which means replaying it consumes your land drop, so the engine only nets you a land per turn if you would otherwise have had nothing to play. Fetches any basic, so its colours resolve against the decklist, not the card.

name: Bad River

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Island or Swamp card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: Produces no mana of its own, so abilities is empty and produces is null. Its colours are a property of the decklist, not the card: it finds any card with the listed land types, which in this pool means the basics and the snow basics. Note basic_only is false because the printed text says card, not basic card, so anything that ever gains one of these types is a legal target. Two timing costs that separate this cycle from the Onslaught fetches: it enters tapped, and cracking it costs {T}, so it cannot be played and cracked on the same turn. The land it finds arrives untapped, which the Onslaught cycle does not, and it costs no life.

name: Flood Plain

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Plains or Island card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bad River. Same cycle.

name: Grasslands

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Forest or Plains card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bad River. Same cycle.

name: Mountain Valley

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Mountain or Forest card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bad River. Same cycle.

name: Rocky Tar Pit

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Swamp or Mountain card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bad River. Same cycle.

name: Crystal Vein
notes: The card that motivated the abilities array. One object, two genuinely different modes: a normal colourless land, or two colourless once. A single amount_per_activation and a single sacrifices_self cannot hold both without lying about one of them.

name: Teferi's Isle

availability.reason: Phasing. It phases out before your untap step on alternating turns, so it is absent for a whole turn cycle at a time.

other_abilities.effect: Phasing.

notes: Two blue for one tap is real acceleration, and the drawbacks are all in timing. It enters tapped, so nothing on turn one. Phasing then takes it away on alternating turns: it phases out before your next untap step, so it does not untap that turn either, and it is usable again the turn after. Reasoning it through, the first turn you can actually tap it is two turns after you play it, and every other turn from there. Legendary, so a second copy is dead. Flagged as the timing I would most like a second pair of eyes on.

name: Coral Atoll
notes: Looks like the Alliances cycle and behaves differently in two ways that matter. The cost is a triggered ability on entering rather than a replacement effect, so the land is briefly on the battlefield and can be responded to. And you return the basic to hand rather than sacrificing it, so the land is not lost, only delayed, and it costs you a land drop later instead of a card. If you cannot or will not pay, this land sacrifices itself. It enters tapped and taps for two, so across its first two turns it is even with a basic, and ahead only from the third turn on.

notes: See Coral Atoll. Same cycle.

notes: See Coral Atoll. Same cycle.

name: Griffin Canyon

notes: Plain colourless land for mana purposes. The Griffin ability costs {T} and competes with the mana ability.

name: Quicksand

other_abilities.effect: Target attacking creature without flying gets -1/-2 until end of turn.

notes: Colourless source that doubles as removal. The sacrifice is on a non-mana ability, which is why other_abilities carries its own sacrifices_self: a deck expecting to use Quicksand as removal should not count it as a land for the rest of the game.

name: Undiscovered Paradise

availability.reason: Instead of untapping it returns to your hand during your next untap step, so each use costs a land drop to replay.

other_abilities.effect: During your next untap step, as you untap your permanents, return this land to its owner's hand.

notes: Enters untapped and taps for any colour immediately, so unlike most fixing in this era it is a genuine turn-one coloured source. The price is that it never untaps; it bounces instead. It is one mana per land drop, so in a deck that wants to develop its mana base every turn it is not free fixing, it is a tax on growth. It can still be tapped during an opponent's turn before it returns.

name: Gemstone Mine
notes: Three activations total, then it sacrifices itself. total_activations is 3 and it is the field that matters more than anything else on this card: treated as an unlimited five-colour source it is one of the best lands in the format, and treated correctly it is three mana spread across a game. The sacrifice happens after the third use, when the last counter is gone, so you do get all three. sacrifices_self is true on the ability because using it is what eventually kills it.

name: Lotus Vale
notes: Three mana of any one colour, all the same colour, which is why produces needs the choice_uniform mode rather than choice: you do not get to spread it across three colours. Entry cost is two untapped lands, and it is a replacement effect, so if you cannot pay it goes straight to the graveyard and you have lost the card and your land drop for nothing. Board arithmetic: two lands and a land drop become one land. Mana per turn is roughly break even, card economy is not, and the whole thing dies to one Wasteland.

name: Scorched Ruins
notes: See Lotus Vale for the entry cost. Four colourless from one land is the largest single activation in the pool so far, and it is colourless, so it accelerates but never fixes.

name: Winding Canyons

other_abilities.effect: You may cast creature spells this turn as though they had flash.

notes: Colourless source. The flash ability costs {T} plus two, so any turn it is used this land is a net drain of two rather than a source.

name: Caldera Lake
notes: Enters tapped and still deals damage, which makes this cycle strictly worse than the Ice Age painlands rather than a variant of them. Same two-ability structure: the colourless mode is free of damage and the coloured mode is not, and the damage is part of that ability's effect rather than a cost, so it cannot be declined once the mode is chosen. The enters_tapped flag is the whole difference and it is the thing that keeps these out of decks that the Ice Age cycle is fine for.

name: Pine Barrens
notes: See Caldera Lake. Same cycle.

name: Salt Flats
notes: See Caldera Lake. Same cycle.

notes: See Caldera Lake. Same cycle.

name: Cinder Marsh

availability.reason: Using this ability leaves the land tapped through your next untap step, so the coloured mode is available every other turn.

notes: Enters untapped, and the colourless mode is completely unrestricted: tap it for {C} every turn forever with no penalty. Only the coloured mode locks it through your next untap step, which is why availability sits on that ability rather than on the card. Rate works out the same as the Ice Age depletion cycle, usable for colour on alternating turns, but the mechanism and the free colourless mode are different and a calculator that treats the two cycles as interchangeable will undercount this one.

name: Rootwater Depths

availability.reason: Using this ability leaves the land tapped through your next untap step, so the coloured mode is available every other turn.

notes: See Cinder Marsh. Same cycle.

notes: See Cinder Marsh. Same cycle.

availability.reason: Using this ability leaves the land tapped through your next untap step, so the coloured mode is available every other turn.

notes: See Cinder Marsh. Same cycle.

name: Ancient Tomb
notes: Two colourless per activation, not one. Amount is the whole point of this card and a classifier that records only colour identity loses it entirely. The 2 damage is part of the ability's effect, not a cost, so it is unavoidable and applies on every activation. Untapped, unconditional, unlimited, so it is real turn-one acceleration and the life total is the only limit.

name: Wasteland

other_abilities.effect: Destroy target nonbasic land.

notes: A colourless source until the moment it is not. The sacrifice is on a non-mana ability, so sacrifices_self is false on the mana ability and true on the other_abilities entry. Behaviourally this is cracked early and proactively, which is what separates it from a card like Barbarian Ring that also sacrifices itself but gets held for a late-game finish. Nothing in the schema encodes that intent; the difference lives in the note and in what the ability actually does.

name: Reflecting Pool

produces.source: any mana type that a land you control could produce

notes: Colours resolve against the board, not the card, so produces gets its own mode rather than a list. Per the Gatherer rulings the ability checks the effects of your other lands' mana abilities but not their costs, their activation conditions, or whether they are untapped: a Homelands castle you cannot afford to activate still feeds it, as does a tapped land. Mana types include colourless, so a land that could add {C} lets this add {C}. What it cannot do is bootstrap. If every other land you control either lacks a mana ability or is another Reflecting Pool, you may activate it and it produces nothing, so a hand of Reflecting Pools makes zero mana. An earlier revision of this note claimed the opposite about conditional lands; it was wrong and the rulings are the reason it changed.

name: Maze of Shadows

other_abilities.effect: Untap target attacking creature with shadow. Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to and dealt by that creature this turn.

notes: Colourless source. The shadow ability costs {T} and competes with the mana ability.

name: Ghost Town

other_abilities.effect: Return this land to its owner's hand. Activate only if it's not your turn.

notes: Colourless source with a free escape hatch from Wasteland and other targeted land removal, usable only on an opponent's turn. Bouncing it is not a mana cost but it does cost your next land drop to replay, and it cannot be used to reset itself on your own turn. Not modelled as an availability restriction because using the mana ability imposes nothing; the bounce is optional and independent.

name: Stalking Stones

other_abilities.effect: Becomes a 3/3 Elemental artifact creature that's still a land. This effect lasts indefinitely.

notes: Colourless source. Animation costs six but does not tap it and is permanent, so unlike the Urza's Legacy manlands it is a one-time investment rather than a per-turn cost. Still a land after animating, so it keeps producing mana.

name: Volrath's Stronghold

other_abilities.effect: Put target creature card from your graveyard on top of your library.

notes: Colourless source. Legendary, so a second copy is dead. The recursion ability costs {T} plus two mana, so a turn spent using it is a turn this land is a net drain rather than a source.

name: City of Traitors

other_abilities.effect: When you play another land, sacrifice this land.

notes: Two colourless with no damage, and the price is that your next land drop kills it. total_activations is null rather than 1 because the count is not fixed: hold your land drops and it keeps producing indefinitely. In practice a deck plays it, uses it, and loses it on the following turn, so a calculator modelling turn-by-turn mana should treat the acceleration as borrowed rather than permanent. Only lands you play trigger it, so opponents cannot force it off and lands put onto the battlefield by effects rather than played do not trigger it either.

name: Drifting Meadow

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: Enters tapped, produces one mana of its colour, and carries an ability that is only usable from hand. Cycling is recorded with type activated_from_hand because it has no bearing on mana once the card is on the battlefield; what it changes is the decision to play the land at all. A calculator counting coloured sources in a decklist should count this at full weight, but a calculator modelling opening hands should know the card has a second use as a cantrip and will sometimes never be a land.

name: Remote Isle

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Drifting Meadow. Same cycle.

name: Polluted Mire

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Drifting Meadow. Same cycle.

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Drifting Meadow. Same cycle.

notes: See Drifting Meadow. Same cycle.

name: Blasted Landscape

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: The colourless member of the cycling cycle and the only one that does not enter tapped. Easy to lose that difference if the six are treated as one group.

name: Gaea's Cradle
notes: first_printing reads JGP because prefer:oldest found the judge promo; the card is legal through Urza's Saga. Amount is 0 by default because with no creatures on the battlefield this taps for nothing at all, and it is not a green source in any meaningful sense until a board exists. That is the entire classification problem here: read as a green land it is a green land, read correctly it is a multiplier on a board state the mana base cannot itself provide. Legendary, so a second copy is dead.

name: Serra's Sanctum
notes: See Gaea's Cradle. Same shape, counting enchantments. Produces nothing on an empty board, so it can never be the white source that lets you cast your first enchantment.

name: Phyrexian Tower
notes: The second ability sacrifices a creature, not the land, so sacrifices_self is false and additional_cost carries the price. Repeatable as long as you have creatures. Like Gaea's Cradle it converts a board into mana, but unlike the Cradle it always has a floor: the colourless mode works on an empty board.

name: Thran Quarry

other_abilities.effect: At the beginning of the end step, if you control no creatures, sacrifice this land.

notes: Untapped, free, any colour, unlimited. On raw mana production this is the best fixing in the pool so far, and the entire cost is the survival clause. The condition on the mana ability is null on purpose: you can tap it for any colour even with no creatures, it simply dies at the end step. Note the trigger checks at the beginning of the end step of every turn, not only yours, so losing your last creature on an opponent's turn kills it before you untap.

name: Shivan Gorge

other_abilities.effect: Deals 1 damage to each opponent.

notes: Colourless source. The damage ability costs {T} plus three mana, so any turn it is used this land is a net drain of three.

name: Faerie Conclave

other_abilities.effect: This land becomes a 2/1 blue Faerie with flying until end of turn. It's still a land.

notes: Enters tapped, so it is never a turn-one source of its colour, and that is the real cost of the cycle. Animation does not tap it, so it can be tapped for mana and animated in the same turn, but the animation cost is mana out of the same pool, and a land that attacks is tapped and produces nothing on your next turn until it untaps. Still a land while animated, so it keeps its mana ability.

name: Forbidding Watchtower

other_abilities.effect: This land becomes a 1/5 white Soldier until end of turn. It's still a land.

notes: See Faerie Conclave. Same cycle.

name: Ghitu Encampment

other_abilities.effect: This land becomes a 2/1 red Warrior with first strike until end of turn. It's still a land.

notes: See Faerie Conclave. Same cycle.

name: Spawning Pool

other_abilities.effect: This land becomes a 1/1 black Skeleton with a regenerate ability until end of turn. It's still a land.

notes: See Faerie Conclave. Same cycle.

name: Treetop Village

other_abilities.effect: This land becomes a 3/3 green Ape with trample until end of turn. It's still a land.

notes: See Faerie Conclave. Same cycle.

name: Yavimaya Hollow

other_abilities.effect: Regenerate target creature.

notes: Colourless source. The regeneration ability costs {T} plus a green mana, so it competes with the mana ability and requires green from elsewhere. Legendary.

name: Peat Bog
notes: Two activations total, then it sacrifices itself, so total_activations is 2 and the lifetime output is four mana. Enters tapped, so nothing on the turn it lands. This is the cycle most likely to be misread as a normal dual-producing land: it taps for two of its colour, which looks like acceleration, but it is a four-mana card that occupies a land slot and then disappears. Contrast the Fallen Empires storage lands, which are also slow but never run out.

name: Hickory Woodlot
notes: See Peat Bog. Same cycle.

name: Remote Farm
notes: See Peat Bog. Same cycle.

name: Sandstone Needle
notes: See Peat Bog. Same cycle.

name: Saprazzan Skerry
notes: See Peat Bog. Same cycle.

name: Fountain of Cho

abilities.cost: {T}, Remove any number of storage counters

variable_amount.accrual: one counter per activation of the charge ability, which taps this land

other_abilities.effect: Put a storage counter on this land.

notes: Storage, but mechanically different from the Fallen Empires cycle and better. Charging is an activated ability that taps the land, so it untaps normally every turn and you simply choose each turn whether to charge or to cash out. The Fallen Empires version instead required you to decline your untap step and only charged at upkeep. Same broad shape, one counter per turn invested, but this one is easier to use and never locks you out of the land. Enters tapped, and amount is 0 by default because with no counters it produces nothing.

name: Mercadian Bazaar

abilities.cost: {T}, Remove any number of storage counters

variable_amount.accrual: one counter per activation of the charge ability, which taps this land

other_abilities.effect: Put a storage counter on this land.

notes: See Fountain of Cho. Same cycle.

name: Rushwood Grove

abilities.cost: {T}, Remove any number of storage counters

variable_amount.accrual: one counter per activation of the charge ability, which taps this land

other_abilities.effect: Put a storage counter on this land.

notes: See Fountain of Cho. Same cycle.

name: Saprazzan Cove

abilities.cost: {T}, Remove any number of storage counters

variable_amount.accrual: one counter per activation of the charge ability, which taps this land

other_abilities.effect: Put a storage counter on this land.

notes: See Fountain of Cho. Same cycle.

name: Subterranean Hangar

abilities.cost: {T}, Remove any number of storage counters

variable_amount.accrual: one counter per activation of the charge ability, which taps this land

other_abilities.effect: Put a storage counter on this land.

notes: See Fountain of Cho. Same cycle.

name: Dust Bowl

other_abilities.effect: Destroy target nonbasic land.

availability.reason: Each activation eats a land from your board, which may be this one.

notes: Colourless source with repeatable land destruction. The sacrifice is a land, not necessarily this one, so sacrifices_self is false; you can feed it another land and keep Dust Bowl. Each use costs three mana plus a land plus this land's tap, so a turn spent activating it is deeply negative on mana.

name: High Market

other_abilities.effect: You gain 1 life.

notes: Colourless source. The sacrifice outlet costs {T} and competes with the mana ability, and it eats a creature rather than the land.

name: Rishadan Port

other_abilities.effect: Tap target land.

notes: Colourless source. Any turn it is used to tap a land it is a net drain of one and produces nothing itself, which is the whole tension in playing it: it is either your mana or their mana, never both.

name: Tower of the Magistrate

other_abilities.effect: Target creature gains protection from artifacts until end of turn.

notes: Colourless source with a non-mana ability that competes for the tap.

name: Henge of Ramos
notes: Same trap as School of the Unseen and the Homelands castles. Reads as five-colour fixing; the coloured mode nets minus one and is not self-sufficient, so it can never produce your first coloured mana.

name: Kor Haven

other_abilities.effect: Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt by target attacking creature this turn.

notes: Colourless source. Legendary. The prevention ability needs white from elsewhere and taps the land, so it is never both mana and defence on the same turn.

name: Rath's Edge

other_abilities.effect: Deals 1 damage to any target.

availability.reason: Each activation eats a land, which may be this one.

notes: See Dust Bowl for the sacrifice-a-land shape. Legendary.

name: Terrain Generator

other_abilities.effect: You may put a basic land card from your hand onto the battlefield tapped.

notes: The fetches object gained a source key for this card. It is not a library search: it puts a basic from your hand onto the battlefield, so it does not thin the deck, does not shuffle, and does nothing if your hand has no basics. It also does not use your land drop, which is the actual reason to play it. Costs two mana plus the tap, and the land arrives tapped, so the turn you use it is a net minus three.

name: Rhystic Cave
notes: Five-colour fixing that any opponent can switch off for one mana, so it should not be counted as a reliable coloured source in any matchup where the opponent holds mana up. The Gatherer ruling of 2004-10-04 says the card carries errata specifically so that it cannot be activated during the casting of a spell or the activation of an ability, which exists to stop an opponent paying {1} and leaving you short mid-cast. The practical consequence is that the mana has to be floated before you begin casting, never tapped in response to your own spell. An earlier revision of this note guessed at a stack-based explanation for that restriction; the ruling is the reason it changed.

name: Wintermoon Mesa

other_abilities.effect: Tap two target lands.

notes: Enters tapped, taps for colourless, and the ability sacrifices it, so it is a land that converts itself into a one-shot double Rishadan Port activation for two mana.

name: Coastal Tower
notes: The simplest shape in the format: enters tapped, taps for one of two colours, no cost, no limit, no condition. Worth recording precisely because it is the baseline every more complicated dual should be compared against. Never a turn-one source of either colour.

name: Elfhame Palace
notes: See Coastal Tower. Same cycle.

name: Salt Marsh
notes: See Coastal Tower. Same cycle.

name: Shivan Oasis
notes: See Coastal Tower. Same cycle.

name: Urborg Volcano
notes: See Coastal Tower. Same cycle.

name: Ancient Spring
notes: The colours of the two abilities do not overlap, which makes this cycle a genuine trap for anything reading mana symbols. Ancient Spring looks like a white-blue-black land. In play it is a blue land that can, exactly once, be cashed in for white and black instead. Note the sacrifice mode produces both symbols together, mode fixed, not a choice between them. Enters tapped, so nothing on turn one, and after the sacrifice you are down a land.

name: Geothermal Crevice
notes: See Ancient Spring. Same cycle, and the same non-overlap between the two abilities.

name: Irrigation Ditch
notes: See Ancient Spring. Same cycle, and the same non-overlap between the two abilities.

name: Sulfur Vent
notes: See Ancient Spring. Same cycle, and the same non-overlap between the two abilities.

name: Tinder Farm
notes: See Ancient Spring. Same cycle, and the same non-overlap between the two abilities.

name: Archaeological Dig
notes: Untapped colourless land that can convert itself once into any single coloured mana. Unlike the Homelands and Masques filters the coloured mode is self-sufficient and nets a full mana, because the price is the land rather than mana. A calculator should count it as one coloured source of every colour, available once.

name: Keldon Necropolis

other_abilities.effect: Deals 2 damage to any target.

notes: Colourless source. Legendary. The damage ability costs five mana plus a creature plus the tap, so it is a late-game mana sink and never competes with using this as a land.

name: Crosis's Catacombs
notes: Two differences from the Visions Karoo cycle that a summary would flatten. These do not enter tapped, and the land you return does not have to be untapped, only a non-Lair land. Against that, they produce one mana of a choice of three rather than two mana, so they fix better and accelerate not at all. The cost is an entering trigger rather than a replacement effect, and failing to pay sacrifices the Lair. Returning a land costs you a future land drop rather than a card, so the deck is down tempo, not resources.

name: Darigaaz's Caldera
notes: See Crosis's Catacombs. Same cycle.

name: Dromar's Cavern
notes: See Crosis's Catacombs. Same cycle.

name: Rith's Grove
notes: See Crosis's Catacombs. Same cycle.

name: Treva's Ruins
notes: See Crosis's Catacombs. Same cycle.

name: Forsaken City

availability.reason: Does not untap during your untap step. Untapping requires exiling a card from your hand at the beginning of your upkeep.

other_abilities.effect: This land doesn't untap during your untap step.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may exile a card from your hand. If you do, untap this land.

notes: Free untapped any-colour mana on the turn it lands, and after that every single use costs a card exiled from hand. The first activation is genuinely free, which is why availability sits on the ability rather than the card and why enters_tapped is false. In a deck that empties its hand this stops untapping entirely and becomes a dead land, so the restriction is not a fixed rate like the depletion lands, it is contingent on a resource the mana base cannot supply.

name: Meteor Crater

produces.source: a colour of a permanent you control

notes: Derived like Reflecting Pool but from a different pool of objects, and much weaker for it. It reads colours off permanents you control, and lands are almost always colourless, so with only lands on the battlefield this produces nothing at all. It cannot help you cast your first spell, only your second onwards, and only in a colour you already have on board. Note it looks at permanents, not lands, so an artifact or a coloured creature enables it.

name: Terminal Moraine

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a basic land card, put that card onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

notes: A colourless land that can convert itself into any basic for two mana. Unlike the Mirage fetches it costs mana and the fetched land arrives tapped, so the turn you use it costs you three mana of tempo for a land that does nothing until next turn. Colours resolve against the decklist.

name: Battlefield Forge
notes: Mechanically identical to the Ice Age painlands, and unlike the Tempest cycle these enter untapped. Free colourless mode with no damage, free coloured mode with 1 damage as part of that ability's effect rather than as a cost. Real turn-one sources of both colours. Together with the Ice Age five these are the backbone of two-colour mana in the format.

name: Caves of Koilos
notes: See Battlefield Forge. Same cycle.

name: Llanowar Wastes
notes: See Battlefield Forge. Same cycle.

name: Shivan Reef
notes: See Battlefield Forge. Same cycle.

name: Yavimaya Coast
notes: See Battlefield Forge. Same cycle.

name: Skycloud Expanse
notes: The card that started this project. One ability, no colourless mode, and it costs a mana to use, so self_sufficient is false and this can never be your first coloured source. Alone on the battlefield it produces nothing at all. What it does do is convert one generic mana into two coloured, which is net plus one and genuinely good in a deck that already has a mana base, so it should not be written off either. produces is mode fixed with both symbols: you get {W} and {U} together, never a choice between them.

name: Darkwater Catacombs
notes: See Skycloud Expanse. Same cycle.

name: Shadowblood Ridge
notes: See Skycloud Expanse. Same cycle.

name: Mossfire Valley
notes: See Skycloud Expanse. Same cycle.

name: Sungrass Prairie
notes: See Skycloud Expanse. Same cycle.

name: Abandoned Outpost
notes: Enters tapped, taps for its colour, or cashes itself in for any single colour. Both modes are free and self-sufficient, so the fixing here is real in a way the Odyssey filter cycle's is not, at the price of the land itself and a turn of tempo.

name: Seafloor Debris
notes: See Abandoned Outpost. Same cycle.

name: Bog Wreckage
notes: See Abandoned Outpost. Same cycle.

name: Ravaged Highlands
notes: See Abandoned Outpost. Same cycle.

name: Timberland Ruins
notes: See Abandoned Outpost. Same cycle.

name: Nomad Stadium

other_abilities.effect: You gain 4 life. Activate only if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.

notes: See Barbarian Ring. Same cycle.

name: Cephalid Coliseum

other_abilities.effect: Target player draws three cards, then discards three cards. Activate only if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.

notes: See Barbarian Ring. Same cycle.

name: Cabal Pit

other_abilities.effect: Target creature gets -2/-2 until end of turn. Activate only if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.

notes: See Barbarian Ring. Same cycle.

name: Barbarian Ring

other_abilities.effect: It deals 2 damage to any target. Activate only if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.

notes: No colourless mode, so unlike every painland cycle every single tap for mana costs you a life. Enters untapped and is otherwise unrestricted. The threshold ability sacrifices it and is gated on seven cards in your graveyard, which is a condition the mana base cannot supply on its own. Behaviourally this is the opposite of Wasteland despite both sacrificing themselves: Wasteland is cracked early and proactively, these are held all game and cashed in late, so a deck expects to use them as lands for many turns first.

name: Centaur Garden

other_abilities.effect: Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn. Activate only if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.

notes: See Barbarian Ring. Same cycle.

name: Crystal Quarry
notes: The five-colour mode is net zero: five mana in, five mana out, one of each colour. It is a colour converter, not acceleration, and it is not self-sufficient. Useful only in a deck that already produces five generic and needs all five colours in one turn, which is a narrow ask.

name: Deserted Temple

other_abilities.effect: Untap target land.

notes: Colourless source whose second ability can target itself, since the tap is paid as a cost before the ability resolves, so for one mana it can reset itself. More usefully it untaps a land that produces more than one mana, which is why it is played alongside Cabal Coffers and the storage lands rather than as a mana source in its own right.

name: Petrified Field

other_abilities.effect: Return target land card from your graveyard to your hand.

notes: Colourless source that trades itself for a land in the graveyard, so it is roughly land-count neutral and card-count neutral, buying back whatever was killed or sacrificed earlier.

name: Tarnished Citadel
notes: Painland structure with a five-colour coloured mode and a much steeper price: 3 damage per activation, part of the ability's effect rather than a cost, so it cannot be declined. The colourless mode is free. Untapped and unlimited, so as raw fixing it is excellent and the life total is the constraint.

name: Cabal Coffers
notes: Not self-sufficient, which is the fact most likely to be missed: it costs {2} to activate, so it can never produce your first black mana and it is net negative until you control three Swamps. It counts Swamps by land type, so Snow-Covered Swamps count and Cabal Coffers itself does not. Amount is 0 by default because the floor is genuinely zero mana returned for two spent.

name: Tainted Field
notes: The colourless mode is free and unconditional; only the coloured mode requires a Swamp, so the condition sits on that ability alone. It checks the Swamp land type, so Snow-Covered Swamp turns it on and this land does not count itself. In a deck with no Swamps at all it is simply a colourless land. Worth noting against Reflecting Pool: the Pool ignores activation conditions, so a Tainted Field with no Swamp in play still lets a Reflecting Pool produce white or black.

name: Tainted Isle
notes: See Tainted Field. Same cycle.

name: Tainted Peak
notes: See Tainted Field. Same cycle.

name: Tainted Wood
notes: See Tainted Field. Same cycle.

name: Krosan Verge

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Forest card and a Plains card, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

notes: The first fetch in the file that gets two lands, and it gets one of each type rather than a choice, which is why the fetches object gained a selection key. Both arrive tapped and it costs {2} plus the land, so the turn you use it is heavily negative and the payoff is a land ahead plus fixed colours from the following turn. Searches by land type, not for basics, so it can find any Forest or Plains card.

name: Nantuko Monastery

other_abilities.effect: This land becomes a 4/4 green and white Insect Monk creature with first strike until end of turn. It's still a land. Activate only if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard.

notes: Colourless source. Animation does not tap it, so mana and animation are compatible on the same turn, but it needs green and white from elsewhere and seven cards in the graveyard.

name: Riftstone Portal

other_abilities.effect: As long as this card is in your graveyard, lands you control have "{T}: Add {G} or {W}."

notes: Unique in this file and the one card here that cannot be evaluated in isolation. On the battlefield it is a colourless land. In the graveyard it grants every land you control the ability to tap for green or white, which means a deck's entire mana base changes colour identity based on whether this card has been discarded or milled. Any calculator that sums per-card colours will be wrong about every other land in the deck while this sits in the graveyard, so global_effect is set to make it findable rather than leaving the fact buried in a note.

name: Bloodstained Mire

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Swamp or Mountain card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: Produces no mana itself, so abilities is empty and produces is null; its colours are a property of the decklist, since Premodern has no dual lands and these can only find what the deck actually plays. Three differences from the Mirage cycle, all of them in this one's favour. It enters untapped, so it can be played and cracked on the same turn. The land it finds arrives untapped. The price is 1 life. Searches by land type rather than for basics, so anything carrying the type is legal, which in this pool means the basics and the snow basics.

name: Flooded Strand

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Plains or Island card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bloodstained Mire. Same cycle.

name: Polluted Delta

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Island or Swamp card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bloodstained Mire. Same cycle.

name: Windswept Heath

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Forest or Plains card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bloodstained Mire. Same cycle.

name: Wooded Foothills

other_abilities.effect: Search your library for a Mountain or Forest card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

notes: See Bloodstained Mire. Same cycle.

name: Barren Moor

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: Same shape as the Urza's Saga cycling lands, with one difference: cycling costs a single mana of this land's own colour rather than {2}. That makes it cheaper in the deck that wants it and unusable in a deck that cannot produce that colour, which is a real constraint on a card whose whole point is flexibility. Enters tapped. Cycling is recorded as activated_from_hand and has no bearing on battlefield mana.

name: Forgotten Cave

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Barren Moor. Same cycle.

name: Lonely Sandbar

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Barren Moor. Same cycle.

name: Secluded Steppe

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Barren Moor. Same cycle.

name: Tranquil Thicket

other_abilities.effect: Discard this card: Draw a card.

notes: See Barren Moor. Same cycle.

name: Contested Cliffs

other_abilities.effect: Target Beast creature you control fights target creature an opponent controls.

notes: Colourless source with a tribal ability that costs coloured mana this land cannot produce, so it never pays for its own ability and any turn it is used it is a net drain. Records as a colourless source only; the colour in the activation cost is a requirement, not production, and is exactly the sort of symbol a text scanner would wrongly count.

name: Daru Encampment

other_abilities.effect: Target Soldier creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Same pattern, different tribe.

name: Goblin Burrows

other_abilities.effect: Target Goblin creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Same pattern, different tribe.

name: Riptide Laboratory

other_abilities.effect: Return target Wizard you control to its owner's hand.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Same pattern, different tribe.

name: Unholy Grotto

other_abilities.effect: Put target Zombie card from your graveyard on top of your library.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Same pattern, different tribe.

name: Wirewood Lodge

other_abilities.effect: Untap target Elf.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Same pattern, different tribe.

name: Seaside Haven

other_abilities.effect: Draw a card.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Colourless source; the ability needs white and blue from elsewhere and eats a Bird, not the land.

name: Starlit Sanctum

other_abilities.effect: You gain life equal to the sacrificed creature's toughness.
Target player loses life equal to the sacrificed creature's power.

notes: See Contested Cliffs. Two separate non-mana abilities in different colours; neither produces mana and both compete with the tap.

name: Grand Coliseum
notes: City of Brass that enters tapped and has a free colourless mode. Two structural differences from City of Brass beyond the tapped entry: the damage here is part of the coloured ability's effect rather than a trigger on becoming tapped, so tapping for colourless costs nothing and taps by opponents' effects cost nothing either. Never a turn-one source of anything.

name: Temple of the False God
notes: Two colourless, and completely dead until you control five lands, itself included. Until then it is not a mana source at all, it is a blank that costs you a land drop, which is why the condition sits on the only ability rather than anywhere softer. Once live it is genuine acceleration with no cost and no limit. self_sufficient is true because activating it needs no mana; the constraint is the board, not the pool.
